svg.title: Four-Week Counterparty and Agent Readiness Roadmap
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-cftc-counterparty-and-agent-readiness; chapter number: 12; title: Four-Week Counterparty and Agent Readiness Roadmap; subtitle: Registration, collateral, funding math and agent controls before capital moves; chart type: timeline_roadmap; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Registration check; deliverable: CFTC registration and NFA membership confirmed through NFA BASIC plus enforcement records; gate: If either registration is missing, walk away; an RFED must hold at least $20 million; week: Week 2; title: FCM due diligence; deliverable: Vanguard checklist run on capital levels, top-tier 1.25 securities, audit and seg-compliance history and custodian rigor; gate: Concentration noted with about 10 firms holding 80% of customer funds; week: Week 3; title: Perpetual funding model; deliverable: Each venue's premium math and observation periods modeled, not a headline rate; gate: Funding every 8 hours capped near 2%, up to 6% per 24 hours, priced before sizing; week: Week 4; title: Agent controls and CCO reporting; deliverable: Risk controls and audit logs outside the agent harness with hard limits and a kill switch; gate: Unredacted home-regulator CCO report or full Reg 3.3 report, never a hybrid; caption: The CFTC stack runs on registration and segregation, and with more than 70% of futures trading automated, the deploying firm is expected to answer for its agents.; assumptions note: Weekly cadence is an organizing assumption; the practitioners reported the checks and figures, not a four-week schedule.; note: Attributed to Brokerchampion (CIinXD9tbVo), CFTC roundtables (yUqRhv7w9Vs, ZEPjpgVSavY, Ckw1w5mSMIQ, ec9Mk3slriY) and A Lawyer In Finance Explains (BO0iMB23sU4).
